clue.text: Suspect agitated, but so dim

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the three words that follow are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is unsettled by a suspicion yet too dim to act on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges BUTSODIM, the letters of 'but so dim', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdoubt is an old verb meaning to have suspicions about, a synonym of suspect as a verb.

clue.text: Dig below in three directions to find native

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece below another is written after it, so the dig word comes after the in word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E, N and E are the compass abbreviations for east, north and east, three directions in a row

explanation.surface: Instructions to an archaeologist to dig down and around to find an indigenous artefact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts DIG under IN in this down entry; then come E, N, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An indigene is a person or thing originating in a place, an aboriginal inhabitant.

clue.text: Point to odd wire worm found in the roof

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it into a new shape, so these letters are recast

parts.note: N, for north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A grub with wiry odd looks has turned up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' recasts N plus the letters of 'odd wire worm' (NODDWIREWORM) into the answer; 'to' is a link. The definition is loose: this kind of window projects from a sloping roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer window is set vertically in a small gable jutting from a pitched roof, so it is located up in the roof.

clue.text: Disentangle some junk no tinker will take

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, the answer running across them

explanation.surface: A tinker so fussy he refuses part of a pile of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks the run inside 'jUNK NOTinker'; 'will take' just links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknot is to undo the knots in something, freeing a tangle.

clue.text: Throw out on to the lawn

explanation.surface: Something hurled out of the window lands on the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To turf out is an idiom for to evict someone; turf is also grass and soil forming a lawn, as in laying turf.

clue.text: Notice shade over first of yews, that's instructive

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece over another comes before it, so the yews letter follows

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a visor shades the eyes

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of yews is used

explanation.surface: A sign of a shadow cast over the churchyard trees is meant to teach something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places AD + VISOR above the Y, from 'first of yews', in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Advisory means giving advice or counsel, so it is informative and guiding.

clue.text: Only a small group involved in riot

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together, so the word riot is rearranged

explanation.surface: Only a handful of people took part in the disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the letters of 'riot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three people, the smallest crowd that counts as a group.

clue.text: A nod is given to the first two escargot plates

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first two signals that only the opening pair of letters of escargot is taken

explanation.surface: A diner nods at a pair of plates of snails in a French restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first two' takes ES from 'escargot'; 'is given to' is read as A + NOD + IS with ES added.
explanation.definitionFit: To anodise is to coat a metal electrolytically with a protective oxide layer, a kind of plating.

clue.text: Go below to find a French nude tangling with Bishop!

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: tangling with suggests the nude word is mixed up together with the bishop letters

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop

explanation.surface: A scandalous scene of a naked French woman getting entangled with a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangling with' mixes the nude letters with RR, the Right Reverend style of a bishop; 'nude' tempts as a picture word but is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To underrun is to pass beneath something, to run under it.

clue.text: Some go with a Durham banker who travels further south

indicators.note: some means only part of the next words is used, here a run across them

explanation.surface: A Durham banker sets off on a trip southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' marks the run inside 'A DURham'. A banker in crosswords is a river, which has banks; the Adur is a river in Sussex, far south of Durham.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so it is a crossword banker, and it flows on its course; the Adur runs through southern England.

clue.text: Dependable fellow who finds Roma difficult

indicators.note: difficult hints that the letters of who finds Roma are troublesome and must be reworked

explanation.surface: A reliable chap struggles with the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges WHOFINDSROMA, all twelve letters of 'who finds Roma'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps promises reliably is called this, an idiom for a trustworthy person.

clue.text: One who fleeces the absentminded

explanation.surface: A sheep shearer is described as distracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a gatherer of wool scraps caught on hedges; the phrase now means a daydreamer whose mind wanders.

clue.text: Painful illness I nurse it fussily

indicators.note: fussily suggests fiddling about, so the letters of I nurse it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient fusses over tending a painful ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the scan stands for 'I', which the letter count needs. 'fussily' rearranges INURSEIT into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuritis is inflammation of a nerve, causing pain and sometimes loss of function.

clue.text: Sarah's around the old city describing the calf

indicators.note: around means the Sarah letters go on either side of the city

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Sarah walks around an ancient city, talking about a young cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Sal is a pet form of Sarah, and Ur, the ancient Mesopotamian city, is a crossword staple; 'calf' means the leg muscle, not a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sural is an anatomical adjective relating to the calf of the leg.

clue.text: Great without harsh smells!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the great letters surround the harsh word

parts.note: OS, outsize, is a clothing abbreviation for great in size
dour means stern or harsh

explanation.surface: A great relief to be free of unpleasant smells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, as in the hymn's 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'; OS is outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents or whiffs, things one smells.

clue.text: Salesman came back with one tiny fairy

indicators.note: came back means the salesman word is read backwards

parts.note: rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesman
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman returns accompanied by a little sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns REP into PER; then I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a beautiful elf-like spirit, a sprite.

clue.text: Hang a weight below wooden board to catch small sea creatures

indicators.note: in a down clue the weight placed below the board follows it

parts.note: a plank is a long wooden board
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Instructions for weighting a board to trap tiny marine life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts TON under PLANK in this down entry; 'Hang' and 'to catch' dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are minute drifting organisms in the ocean, plants and animals alike.

clue.text: Join the railway after a month

indicators.note: after means the railway letters come following the month

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation for March
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone joins the railway company a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join' could be a verb for signing up, but it means wed; 'after' places the railway abbreviation behind the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to unite two people in wedlock, so to unite or link.

clue.text: Fire raisers in here fight after marriage

indicators.note: after means the fight word comes behind the marriage word

parts.note: a match is a marriage, as in a good match
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Arsonists come to blows once the wedding is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire raisers' looks like arsonists; they are matches, kept in this container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small box holds matches, which raise fire when struck.

clue.text: Gallery full of figureheads

explanation.surface: An art gallery displays carved ships' figureheads.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the gods is the highest gallery, with the cheapest seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The gods is the top balcony of a theatre; gods are also deities, idol figures at the head of worship.

clue.text: Party member ensures a fair degree of equality

definitions.text: ensures a fair degree of equality

explanation.surface: A politician claims to secure fairness for all.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US, a Democrat belongs to the Democratic Party; lower case, a democrat champions equal rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Democratic Party, and a believer in rule by the people with equal rights for all.

clue.text: Good chap runs after flustered maid at the heart of things

indicators.note: runs after means the good chap letters follow the rearranged maid
flustered means agitated, so the maid letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: St, saint, is a crossword good person

explanation.surface: A kind man chases a flustered maid through the middle of the action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flustered' signals the anagram; 'runs after' sets the saint behind it, 'runs' giving no R. 'at the heart of things' means among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means in the middle of, among the surrounding things.

clue.text: Limit fee to three score and ten perhaps

indicators.note: to here works as a signal of change, the letters of limit fee being turned into something else

explanation.surface: A request to cap a charge at seventy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a thin anagram signal: LIMITFEE rearranged gives the answer. Three score and ten, seventy years, is the biblical span of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalm 90 gives the span of a human life as seventy years, an example of a life's duration.

clue.text: Girl left to construct a pretty display

definitions.note: a noun phrase, while the answer is an adjective describing such a display of flowers

parts.note: Flora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl leaves to arrange an attractive show.
explanation.walkthrough: FLORA + L; 'to construct' links the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means made of flowers, as a bright arrangement of blooms is.

clue.text: Be aware of events on the field

definitions.text: Be aware of events on the field

parts.words: Be aware of events on the field
parts.note: an idiom for understanding a situation, read literally as knowing the points tally of a sports match

explanation.surface: A spectator keeps track of what happens in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to understand the real situation; on a sports field it literally means knowing the points.

clue.text: Picks a spot of bother

indicators.note: of bother suggests the letters of spot are put into disarray

explanation.surface: Someone chooses to get into a little trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a spot of bother' is a British idiom for a minor trouble; 'of bother' rearranges SPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opts is a synonym for chooses.

clue.text: Could be 3 band

explanation.surface: A belt that might be a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is 3-down: a sash window is one with sliding frames, so a sash could be that window type.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash window is a common style for the window in 3-down; a sash is also a sash belt or strip of fabric worn across the body.

clue.text: Uncommon or cooked

explanation.surface: Is the steak unusual or well done?
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is ironic: rare meat is only lightly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means scarce, and describes meat cooked only briefly so it stays red inside.

clue.text: Exits to the open air

explanation.surface: Doors leading out into the fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, out doors are exits; as one word it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors out are exits; as an adverb the word means outside in the fresh air.

clue.text: Gaity-the Spring term has it!

indicators.note: has means the term holds the other word inside it

parts.note: Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford University and in the law courts
taken as written

explanation.surface: The spring term is full of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary is the name of the spring term at Oxford and the Inns of Court; 'has' signals holding the word inside. 'Gaity' is printed for gaiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is boisterous merriment and laughter, the same as gaiety.
